land.text: 'in 1472, James declared the Norðreyjar to be forfeit': Orkney and Shetland pass to the Scottish crown

correction.text: the Northern Isles: Orkney and Shetland (the Norðreyjar)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no earldom. Orkney and Shetland sit inside its Old Kingdom of Norway shapes from 866 (the Norway dossier records the 875 annexation and puts the earldom's mainland piece, Caithness and Sutherland, in Norway too). The page says the mainland parts 'were subject to the kings of Alba', without a year, so they are left out of this shape.

ledger.note: c. 872: the earldom is created. Infobox 'Creation date: c. 872'; the page's table of Norse jarls gives c. 892 and says Rognvald Eysteinsson 'is sometimes credited with being the founder of the jarldom of Orkney'; Torf-Einarr 'may be regarded as the first historical earl of Orkney' (c. 895-910). The year is approximate and the page gives two.

region.text: Orkney, the earldom passing to a Scottish dynasty

ledger.note: 1232: a Scottish family takes the earldom. 'In 1232, a Scottish dynasty descended from the mormaers of Angus replaced the previous family'; the Norse line ended when Jarl Magnus II was granted his title by Haakon IV (c. 1236 on the page's table).
2 August 1379: 'the jarldom was granted to another grandson of Maol Íosa, Henry Sinclair, by Haakon VI on 2 August 1379'; table rule 1379 to 1401.

region.text: Orkney and Shetland, forfeit to the Scottish crown

ledger.note: 1472: the earldom ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1472'; William's quitclaim came in 1470 (not 1468-69) after Christian I 'pledged the Norðreyjar as security for his promise', and 'in 1472, James declared the Norðreyjar to be forfeit'.

certainty.note: The page gives the islands, no frontier or date for the mainland parts.

notes: Vassalage: 'the status of the rulers of the Northern Isles as Norwegian vassals was formalised in 1195' (the page); that is a relation recorded from Norway's side (kingdom 'old-kingdom-of-norway' has the islands as a 875 gain, with no 1195 vassal_start) and is not repeated here. Others on the page: Thorfinn the Mighty sole ruler c. 1036-c. 1046 and alone to c. 1064; Magnus Erlendsson martyred c. 1115; Rognvald Kali Kolsson from 1136; Harald Maddadsson from 1138 and alone 1158-1191 (the page does not mention Caithness for him). The mainland: 'those parts of their territory in what is now mainland Scotland (i.e. Caithness and Sutherland) were subject to the kings of Alba', undated, so the mainland is not drawn. Later creations: 1581 (forfeited 1614) and 1696 (extant). Overlap: kingdom-of-scotland has the 1472 gain from the Kalmar Union; both are consistent. The page budget was one page (the Orkney facts also sit on the Norway and Scotland dossiers).
